description: Machine-readable feature state list. Single source of truth for scope. State transitions are gated by verification: a feature only becomes 'passing' when its verification command actually passes. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: CLI accepts `npx humb <database-url>`, auto-detects the database engine from the target (Postgres today), and starts the local server.
features.evidence: commit 9c37ec2 (PR #3): pnpm --filter humb test passes (7/7, packages/cli/src/index.test.ts) on 2026-07-01. Manually re-verified end to end against a real Postgres container: `HUMB_PORT=7799 humb <url>` listened on 7799 (env var previously silently ignored, now fixed via resolvePort), and `GET /` served the built apps/web UI (previously 404'd; fixed via static serving in packages/server) with `GET /api/health` reporting `connected`.

features.behavior: Launching Humb opens the browser UI which shows the database connection status.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container. Fixed a real infra gap along the way: Playwright's webServer only ran `vite preview` (no backend), so /api/health always failed - replaced with e2e/server.ts, which starts the real Humb server (API + built web app on one port, matching a real `npx humb <url>` launch) and connects to Postgres only when HUMB_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set.

features.behavior: Postgres adapter introspects schemas, tables, columns, indexes, and row counts.
features.evidence: commit 4ec7345 (PR #4): pnpm --filter @humbdb/db-postgres test passed (16/16) on 2026-07-01, including new integration tests (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) against a real Postgres container that previously did not exist for getOverview/getTable/getRows/runReadOnlyQuery. Auditing against the full spec found schemas/tables/columns were covered but indexes and row counts were entirely unimplemented (missing from @humbdb/core's TableMetadata contract and the adapter) - added IndexMetadata to @humbdb/core, index introspection via pg_index/pg_class/pg_attribute, and an approximate row count via pg_class.reltuples with a COUNT(*) fallback for never-analyzed tables (reltuples is -1 until ANALYZE runs). Manually re-verified end to end: GET /api/tables/public/humb_demo_users returned real indexes (with a genuine string[] columns array, not the raw Postgres array-literal string node-postgres returns for untyped array columns - caught and fixed via an explicit ::text cast) and rowCount 3. Package later renamed/moved packages/db-postgres -> packages/drivers/postgres (@humbdb/postgres) in commit cc3db12 (PR #5) as part of an architecture reorganization; re-verified the same 16/16 pass at the new location and updated this verification command accordingly.

features.behavior: UI shows a database navigation tree (schemas/tables) and table metadata.
features.evidence: commit ec9ebf2 (PR #6): pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01: added SchemaTree/TableDetail components (@humbdb/ui), api/hooks (apps/web), wired into App.tsx. The connect-and-inspect journey now actually clicks the fixture table in the nav tree and asserts a column name is visible (previously only asserted the table name appeared as text, which would have passed without real interaction) - strengthened per the goal-driven-execution rule rather than leaving a superficial check.

features.behavior: UI displays a paginated page of rows for a selected table.
features.evidence: commit 1f779da: pnpm test:e2e:full passes (1/1) on 2026-07-01 against a real Postgres container: added RowsTable (@humbdb/ui), api/rows.ts + useRows hook (apps/web, using TanStack Query's keepPreviousData to avoid flicker between pages), wired into App.tsx below TableDetail with Previous/Next controls. "Can go next" uses a simple rows.length === pageSize heuristic (no exact total count from the backend) - manually verified the boundary is correct via curl with page=0/1 at pageSize=2 against the 3-row fixture. The connect-and-inspect journey now asserts real fixture row values (ada@example.com, grace@example.com) are visible, not just presence of a table.

features.behavior: Read-only SQL query runner executes SELECT-style statements and rejects mutations.
features.evidence: commit c049110: pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test (24/24) and pnpm --filter @humbdb/server test (8/8) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing found a real, exploitable security bug: assertReadOnly only checked the leading keyword, so a writable CTE (`WITH deleted AS (DELETE FROM t RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM deleted`) starts with the allowed "with" keyword but actually deletes data - confirmed this executed a real DELETE through the adapter against a live table before fixing it. Fixed with two layers: assertReadOnly now scans the whole statement (literals/identifiers stripped first) for forbidden keywords anywhere, not just leading; and runReadOnlyQuery now runs inside a real Postgres READ ONLY transaction as the authoritative backstop - proved this independently with a test hiding a DELETE inside a plpgsql function call, which no string check could ever catch. Also fixed a rejected query returning HTTP 500 instead of 400 (moved ReadOnlyViolationError to @humbdb/driver-contract so packages/server can catch it without depending on a concrete engine). Built the missing UI (QueryRunner in @humbdb/ui, wired via apps/web) and manually verified success/rejection/writable-CTE cases through the real HTTP path against a live Postgres container.

features.behavior: Local server exposes health and runtime diagnostics endpoints for agent verification.
features.evidence: commit 5259102: pnpm --filter @humbdb/server test (8/8) and pnpm --filter @humbdb/postgres test (25/25) pass on 2026-07-01. Auditing /api/health (built in F001) against the full spec found a real bug, not just a coverage gap: node-postgres's Pool emits an unhandled "error" event when an idle client's connection is severed by the database (restart, network blip, admin kill) - confirmed live by starting the CLI against a real Postgres container, stopping the container mid-session, and watching the entire Node process crash instead of /api/health ever reporting "disconnected". Fixed by attaching pool.on("error", ...) in packages/drivers/postgres/src/index.ts's connect() to log instead of crash. Re-verified live: after the fix, killing the database leaves the server up and /api/health correctly returns database: "disconnected"; a subsequent SIGINT still shuts down cleanly. Added a regression test (postgres-adapter.integration.test.ts) that reproduces the exact failure via pg_terminate_backend on an idle pooled connection against a real database - confirmed it fails (uncaught exception) without the fix and passes with it.

Also validates the driver-plugin architecture: a second engine is what actually proves packages/drivers/<engine> is reusable, not just designed to look reusable. Playwright coverage of the SQLite journey is split out as F011 (see docs/PLANS.md's rule on splitting oversized work) - this entry covers the backend adapter + CLI wiring, verified live end to end via the real HTTP path, not just package tests.

features.evidence: commit 9ccde55: new packages/drivers/mysql (@humbdb/mysql) implements DatabaseAdapter on mysql2/promise, mirroring @humbdb/postgres's shape - backtick identifier quoting (MySQL's own dialect, kept local to this package per ARCHITECTURE.md), information_schema introspection (explicit lowercase column aliases, since MySQL's server always returns information_schema results in UPPERCASE regardless of how the query is written - caught live via a real container), exact COUNT(*) row counts per spec, and a START TRANSACTION READ ONLY backstop in runReadOnlyQuery proven live by opening that same transaction directly (bypassing the adapter and assertReadOnly) and confirming MySQL itself still refuses a write. pool.on('error', ...) attached to the promise pool's underlying callback pool prevents a dropped idle connection from crashing the process (F007 precedent) - verified live via a real container. packages/core gained mysql:// detection; packages/cli wired mysqlAdapterFactory in. New e2e 'mysql' Playwright project/webServer; connect-and-inspect/query-history/sql-editor-autocomplete specs extended to a real 3-way branch. Found and fixed two real bugs while wiring this up: (1) every e2e webServer instance inherits every test-DB env var simultaneously, so the old 'whichever var is truthy' selection in e2e/server.ts was silently routing the new 'mysql' project to SQLite instead - fixed with an explicit HUMB_E2E_ENGINE env var per webServer entry, confirmed live via direct health-endpoint checks per port; (2) a real, reproduced concurrency bug in setupSqliteFixture (DROP+CREATE not race-safe across concurrent Playwright workers, once a third engine project pushed total parallelism higher) - fixed the same way F012 fixed the analogous Postgres bug, wrapping the whole sequence in one transaction with a busy_timeout, confirmed via 4 repeated full-parallelism runs with zero flakes afterward. Also needed a tsconfig.base.json '@humbdb/mysql' paths entry (tsx/tsc resolve every workspace package straight to source this way) and turbo.json's 'test' task env allowlist to include HUMB_TEST_MYSQL_URL. pnpm --filter @humbdb/mysql test (13/13, unit + integration against a real MySQL 8 container) and pnpm check (full monorepo) both pass; pnpm test:e2e:full (all three engine projects, run 4x) and pnpm test:e2e pass with zero flakes. Manually verified live via Preview against a real MySQL container with an FK-constrained fixture: Schema tab shows PK/FK badges correctly, Tables tab paginates rows, and the SQL Editor runs a query using a double-quoted string value (MySQL's own default dialect behavior, no adapter-side coercion needed - confirmed this is genuinely different from F018's Postgres-only fix).

features.behavior: MongoDB as a fourth engine (npx humb mongodb://...), deliberately scoped to basic read-only browsing only: databases as schemas, collections as tables, best-effort sampled field lists per collection, paginated document browsing (each page's columns are the union of fields observed on that page, not just a table-level sample). No query runner (the SQL Editor tab is not usable against a Mongo connection) and no driver-level read-only backstop - enforced instead by the adapter's code never calling any Mongo write API, explicitly weaker than every other engine's guarantee (see docs/product-specs/connect-and-inspect-mongodb.md's "Read-only enforcement" section). Depends on F016 (structured-cell viewer) shipping first - nested document fields are unusable as flat JSON text.

features.behavior: A single Fastify setErrorHandler normalizes every route's uncaught-error response into one consistent { error: string } shape (the real underlying message, not Fastify's generic reason phrase) - found a real bug while testing F012: POST /api/query only special-cased ReadOnlyViolationError, so any other failure (e.g. a bad table name) fell through to Fastify's default handler, and the frontend read the wrong field (body.error, literally "Internal Server Error") instead of the real Postgres message sitting in body.message. New shared ErrorState UI component (packages/ui) - occupies the same visual footprint the loaded view would, message centered, Retry action - replaces today's inconsistent inline error text across QueryRunner's result area, RowsTable, SchemaGrid, FilesBrowser, and ConsoleLog. features.behavior: A developer can switch the running Humb instance to a different database connection from the title bar's Settings drawer, without restarting the CLI - a new POST /api/connect endpoint swaps the server's live adapter/target, and apps/web resets cached state (overview/tables/rows/console, selected table, page) for the new connection.
features.evidence: commit 6d55edd: CreateServerOptions gains an optional adapterFactories field; when provided, a new POST /api/connect endpoint parses the target, resolves+connects a new adapter, and only swaps it in (disconnecting the old adapter) once a ping confirms the new one is live - a bad target never leaves the developer with no connection. adapter/target became mutable closure state (were const-destructured) so every route sees a switch immediately. packages/cli's main() and e2e/server.ts both pass the full factory list so the real CLI and Preview/e2e verification get this by default. The title bar's previously-disabled Settings button now opens a ConnectDrawer (same right-anchored pattern as QueryHistoryDrawer/CellValueDrawer) showing the current target, a connect form, and up to 5 recent targets (localStorage-backed, capped list, most-recent-first). useConnect invalidates every React Query cache on success; App.tsx resets the selected table/page; the SQL Editor's draft is deliberately left untouched. A real bug was caught live during verification: connecting to an unreachable host throws Node's AggregateError, whose own .message is empty (the real reason is in .errors[0]) - the drawer initially showed a blank error instead of "connect ECONNREFUSED ...". Fixed via a new describeError() helper (also applied to the pre-existing /api/health ping-failure path, which had the same latent bug) plus a regression test reproducing the exact AggregateError shape. Verified live via Preview against a real docker-compose Postgres+MySQL stack: switched a running instance from Postgres to MySQL and back (a different engine entirely, not just a different database - sidebar, engine version, and table list all updated with no restart), confirmed a failed switch attempt (bad host) leaves the old connection fully queryable with a real error message shown, and confirmed the recent-targets list populates and reconnects correctly. pnpm check (format/lint/typecheck/test/build/check:state) and pnpm test:e2e/test:e2e:full both pass against a real docker-compose Postgres+MySQL+Mongo stack (52/52 server tests including 6 new F064 cases, 10/10 e2e @full non-skipped, 3/3 @smoke).

features.behavior: Clicking a RowsTable column header sorts the entire table (via a new sortColumn/sortDirection param on GET /api/tables/:schema/:table/rows and each engine's getRows), not just the currently loaded page, with the sort column validated server-side against the table's real columns.
